description_full: T. Rowe Price Group, Inc. is a publicly owned investment manager. The firm provides its services to individuals, institutional investors, retirement plans, financial intermediaries, and institutions. It launches and manages equity and fixed income mutual funds. The firm invests in the public equity and fixed income markets across the globe. It employs fundamental and quantitative analysis with a bottom-up approach. The firm utilizes in-house and external research to make its investments. It employs socially responsible investing with a focus on environmental, social, and governance issues. It makes investment in late-stage venture capital transactions and usually invests between $3 million and $5 million. The firm was previously known as T. Rowe Group, Inc. and T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc. T. Rowe Price Group, Inc. was founded in 1937 and is based in Baltimore, Maryland, with additional offices in North America, Europe, Asia, Australia.
ceo_bio: Mr. Robert W. Sharps C.F.A., CPA | CEO & Chair of the Board | Age 54 | Compensation: $8.8M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 7K people. Revenue per employee of $957K ranks in the above the sector median among Financial Services peers, with revenue growing 9%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $194K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $28K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 9× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: T. Rowe Price Group, Inc. is a large-cap financial services business with a $21.5B market cap on $7.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 23% against a 12% cost of capital — a 12-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 100% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.5B in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.84× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 8.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
